diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then average velocity $w(\cdot;r,t)$ for $0\le r\le t\le 1$ is globally Lipschitz

issues.failure_explanation: The definition divides by t-r, but the algorithms and theorem explicitly permit r=t. On that diagonal the displayed quotient is 0/0, and no limiting definition is supplied.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require r<t wherever the quotient is used, or define w_{t,t} by the appropriate limiting instantaneous velocity and verify that the extension has the claimed regularity.
issues.overall_effect: The averaged velocity and regression target are not defined for every time pair allowed by the stated procedures, and the theorem's r=t case is invalid as written.
issues.title: Average velocity is undefined on the permitted diagonal r=t
issues.why_classification: A standard local diagonal convention or strict inequality resolves the defect without changing the method, rates, or substantive scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Thus, Encode-only and Encode--Decode correspond to the same conditional-mean principle, but in different geometries:

issues.failure_explanation: The regression target is not a fixed random variable: it contains the current network w_theta and its JVP. Stop-gradient changes differentiation through the target but does not make its numerical value independent of theta. Therefore the ordinary fixed-target MSE theorem does not establish that a population minimizer of the stated training problem is the displayed conditional mean; at most, a theta-dependent conditional projection identity holds pointwise, and a fixed-point or optimization argument is still needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Define the linear map on the distribution space $\mathcal{H}^{-s}$ by
\[
\mathcal{T}:\mathcal{H}^{-s}\to \mathcal{H}^{-s}, \quad \mathcal{T}(\xi)=C^{1/2}\xi,
\]
and cannot be realized as a continuous or Lipschitz map $\mathcal{H}\to\mathcal{H}$.

issues.failure_explanation: Mutual singularity of source and target measures does not obstruct deterministic pushforwards. Indeed, the paper itself constructs T=C^{1/2} on the common space H^{-s}; because C^{1/2} is a bounded diagonal operator there, this is a continuous/Lipschitz transport from white noise to the trace-class Gaussian. Moreover, the same formula is a bounded continuous map H to H, contrary to the example's literal last claim, although white noise is not a probability measure on that smaller domain. The actual issue is the choice of state space, not singularity ruling out regular transport.

failure_location.quote:
This support mismatch manifests as mutual singularity on a distribution space $\mathcal{H}^{-s}$,
and rules out any regular deterministic one-step transport realized as a map $\mathcal{H}\to\mathcal{H}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must formulate a meaningful regularity class and common source/target state space, then prove an obstruction in that class. Otherwise the claimed impossibility must be withdrawn and replaced by the narrower fact that white noise is not H-valued.
issues.overall_effect: The proposition proving singularity remains valid, but it does not justify the paper's central claimed obstruction to white-reference one-step transports. Corresponding claims in the abstract, introduction, theory discussion, and conclusion are overstated.
issues.title: Mutual singularity does not rule out a regular deterministic transport
issues.why_classification: The source supplies a regular transport on the natural common distribution space, so preserving the advertised white-noise obstruction requires essentially new theory; the available repair materially weakens a central claimed contribution.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In practice, we truncate to $N_{\mathrm{KL}}=64$ KL coefficients (real Fourier basis), ordered by increasing $|k|^2$.
We fix the gauge by setting $\hat\psi(0)=0$.

issues.failure_explanation: On a periodic domain, -Delta psi=u is solvable only when u has zero spatial mean. The stated periodic GRF has a nonzero-variance k=0 coefficient, and ordering retained modes by increasing |k|^2 includes that constant mode. Setting the zero Fourier coefficient of psi to zero fixes a gauge but does not solve the k=0 equation when the sampled vorticity has nonzero mean.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Impose a mean-zero vorticity prior by excluding or conditioning out the k=0 coefficient, and state the corresponding mean-zero compatibility condition throughout the Navier–Stokes setup.
issues.overall_effect: The stated Navier–Stokes forward model is not defined for almost every draw from the specified prior, so its data-generation and posterior construction are inconsistent unless the constant mode was silently removed.
issues.title: The Navier–Stokes prior permits vorticity for which the streamfunction equation is unsolvable
issues.why_classification: Removing one constant Fourier mode is a standard local compatibility condition and preserves the model, numerical method, and advertised experimental regime.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Although Theorem~\ref{thm:dimfree_lip_velocity} is stated and proved in finite dimensions in \cite{meng2025pathway},
its Lipschitz bound involves constants that are independent of the ambient dimension.
We therefore interpret it as a function-space stability statement.

issues.failure_explanation: The cited input is expressly only finite-dimensional. A dimension-independent Lipschitz estimate alone does not construct an infinite-dimensional Föllmer velocity, establish convergence of finite-dimensional velocities, identify the limiting transport, or show that the limit retains the bound. The source provides only an interpretation, not the nontrivial limiting argument required for the theorem on a separable Hilbert space.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must construct the infinite-dimensional velocity as a suitable limit and prove existence, identification, and preservation of the dimension-free Lipschitz estimate.

issues.title: A finite-dimensional Föllmer theorem is asserted on function space without a limiting argument
issues.why_classification: Establishing an infinite-dimensional limit requires new proof architecture. Without it, the paper loses its principal function-space regularity guarantee.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed estimate would follow for the pointwise temporal average (t-r)^{-1} integral v(tau,z) d tau with a fixed spatial argument z. The paper instead defines w by evaluating v along paths z_tau. Comparing w at two endpoint states therefore also requires control of how the corresponding paths depend on those endpoints; the integral of the spatial Lipschitz constants alone does not supply that control. In addition, the theorem invokes a Föllmer velocity while the algorithmic definition uses the velocity of an independently coupled linear interpolation, and no identification between these fields is proved.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must define the averaged velocity as a function of a specified endpoint, control the associated path/flow dependence, and connect the Föllmer velocity to the linear-interpolation Mean-Flow field used by the sampler.
issues.overall_effect: Even if the infinite-dimensional Föllmer theorem were supplied, the asserted L0/2 bound for the averaged Mean-Flow velocity and the resulting one-step Lipschitz guarantee would still not follow.
issues.title: The Lipschitz bound averages velocities at fixed points rather than along the Mean-Flow paths
issues.why_classification: The missing pathwise and velocity-identification arguments are central to the one-step regularity theorem and require new proof architecture rather than a local estimate.
